chapter: Dancing schools, Sapiro and Jelly Roll Morton
title: Rose Danceland: Charlie Skeets, the Benfords, and Jelly Roll's arrival
summary: After the Bamboo Inn he worked at Rose Danceland on 125th Street, a bigger dancing school whose leadership passed from Charlie Skeets through Tommy and Bill Benford to Jelly Roll Morton.

story.theme_name: Dance halls, lake camps and riverboat bandstands
story.community_name: Dance halls, lake resorts and where bands played

blocks.x: Yeah. So that brings us to when it folded, then I went to work at Rose Danceland, which was at 125th Street and 7th Avenue.
Oh, with Jelly Roll Morton?

Well, that was a funny type of job, because we were playing and from time to time different people became the leader. When I went there it was Charlie Skeets. Charlie Skeets was a piano player from Brooklyn, and he had a very good band sometime before that, because I'd heard them from Brooklyn, he had all Brooklyn fellows in there. A couple of them played with Claude Hopkins later on. But he had the band and he left and Tommy Benford was the drummer in the band. Tommy Benford and his brother Bill Benford was the bass player. And Bill Benford was the -- after Charlie Skeets left, got fired or something or other, Tommy Benford took over. Bill Benford, his brother, his older brother, took over. He was the boss for awhile. Then Jelly Roll Morton came.
Jelly Roll Morton came -- what about Billy Cato? Is that -- he had nothing to do with the Rose Danceland, or --
No, Billy Cato's later on.
Oh.
Later on. That was another dancing school. See, I worked in dancing -- and I liked the dancing schools.
Rose Danceland, was that a dancing school, like the 116th Street Dancing School?
Yeah. Yeah. Only it was on a higher level. It was more elaborate and bigger, more girls, and a bigger band and everything, you know, on a larger scale.
Where was it located?
125th Street and 7th Avenue. You know where that cigar store is?
Yes.
The cigar store's still there. It was right upstairs, over that. Yeah.
So it was right next to the -- it was near -- next to the Alhambra.
Yeah. Well, the Alhambra's on the corner of 126th Street.
Yeah.
Yeah.
But that block, the same block.
Yeah. Yeah. I worked the Alhambra too. I worked there with Chick Webb.
But -- okay, so you -- how long were you there, at Rose Danceland?
Oh, how long was I there? My time, you know, gets -- I forget.
Well, I have it that you were with Charlie Skeets in '27 and that you worked with Jelly Roll Morton in the summer of '28. So would that be part of '27 and into '28?
Yeah, I guess so, yeah.
